It ran 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-06 and stopped there: 4,188 of 58,961 files copied to `I:\My Drive\Unsilenced archive backup`, 1,450 failed, the last lines Google's rate limit (`tmp/unsilenced-titles/run.log` in kop-pipeline); nothing has run since. Restart it with `Start-Process python -ArgumentList 'scripts/unsilenced-backup.py','run' -WindowStyle Hidden` in kop-pipeline: it resumes, retries the failed ones, and pauses on its own if C: drops under 4 GB (Drive for desktop stages uploads there; 12 GB free on 2026-10-25). Losing the state is fine: `run` counts a copy already on disk whose md5 matches as done, so it only re-reads those 4,218 to check them. The list has to come down from the server first: `scp -i ~/.ssh/kop_nixihost -P 1157 kidsover@dfw-s07.nixihost.com:kop-import/unsilenced/files.jsonl ../kop-pipeline/tmp/unsilenced/` (if `check/files.jsonl` there is newer, from the monthly cron, take that one instead).

items.lead: Utah findings stored without the state's statement
items.text: **Utah findings stored without the state's statement** (found 2026-11-03, About rewrite pilot, Lava Heights): of the 411 UT reports in prod with a finding, 181 (2023-26, all inspection types) hold only the rule title in `inspection_reports.raw_content` (e.g. report 75584: "R380-80-5(10): Services and supervision..."); the other 230 carry the state's "out of compliance... During the inspection..." text. Utah's API (`cclapi.dlbc.utah.gov/api/public/facilities/<id>`) gives `declarativeStatement`, `noncomplianceLevel`, `cmpAmount` and `correctionAction` for every finding, checklist or not. Find why the UT scraper drops it for those 181 and backfill them. (kop-data's `ut_reports.json`, last updated 2025-10-17, is the old static file; the site reads prod, which has the 2026 inspections.) - **Cause (2026-11-03)**: Utah renamed the field `findingText` -> `declarativeStatement` (the March 2026 export `ut_reports_03182026.json` still has `findingText` on every finding); `utah_citation_scraper.py` read only `findingText`, and its Sept 28 and Nov 1 runs re-posted with the title alone (`inspections-write.php` overwrites `raw_content` on the duplicate key). Counting every row with a title-only line it is **212** rows, not 181. items.lead: Vet the names in unlinked articles: link, create a record, or leave out (planned 2026-10-28)
items.text: **Vet the names in unlinked articles: link, create a record, or leave out (planned 2026-10-28)**. On the 2026-10-27 mirror 191 approved articles link to no facility: 275 names, and 69 articles with no names at all. Triage without AI: 26 names (23 articles) already match a record exactly; 45 match a company (on its /operator/ page after item 21); 158 have look-alike records ("Sununu Youth Services Center" vs "John H. Sununu Youth Services Center", "Discovery Ranch Academy" vs "Discovery Ranch"); 46 have none. Scope rules every step follows: ORR shelters and juvenile detention are TTI; foster care, adult DD homes, nursing homes, general hospitals and state agencies are not; 18+ programs go to young adult programs, never facilities; a name belongs to its own years and operator (a rename is another era, not a new record). Steps (lead = Opus, the session running it): 0. **Code, no AI: links follow records created later.** Done 2026-10-28: `kop_facdisc_relink_resolved()` (inc/facility-discovery.php) runs after each hourly scan and resyncs up to 100 live articles naming a record or company by exact name that they are not linked to; the one-time admin_init pass `kop_facdisc_maybe_relink()` (option `kop_facdisc_relink` = 1, owner approved) takes them all and logs news id => ids gained in `kop_facdisc_relink_log`. On the 2026-10-27 mirror: 70 articles, 51 facility + 24 company links. - Ran on production 2026-10-28 (e603be26, admin-ajax): `kop_facdisc_relink_log` lists 70 articles, the same as the mirror; spot-checked links #106 -> 100185, #334 -> 11049, #267 -> company 27 are there. - **Bare names beside "(...)" records (owner decides)**: 43 records share their exact name with a record that adds a "(...)" ("Lakeside Academy" UT beside "Lakeside Academy (MI)" and "(MN)"; "Hyde School" ME beside "(CT)"; "Behavior Research Institute" CA beside "(Providence)"). The exact match always takes the bare one, so a save links every "Lakeside Academy" article, Kalamazoo's included, to Utah: 58 mentioned links on live articles (Hyde 23, Lakeside 12, BRI 8, Embark 4). The relink holds those articles back, so they stay in the vetting worklist with the look-alikes. Open: make a bare name that a "(...)" sibling shares ambiguous in `kop_build_facility_alias_index()` (save-time too; a resync would then take those 58 links off, the right ones with the wrong), or rename the bare records with their own qualifier. - Worklist: `scripts/news-name-vetting.php` (2026-10-28, on prod tables pulled that day): 184 live articles link to no facility; 266 names: 46 on a company page, 171 with look-alikes, 49 with none; 71 articles list no name; 96 articles to sort in 5 batches of 20, plus 14 whose names an agent pulled from title and summary (batch 6; 50 of the 71 name nothing). Step 1 done: 248 verdicts (same_record 19, other_era 5, new_facility 23, Indian boarding schools 9 (Indigenous Schools, not facilities), new_company 34, out_of_scope 126, not_a_program 32). Script check: every id is a look-alike; 1 quote off by an apostrophe. But 134 verdicts have no quote and 149 are low confidence: the names came from article bodies the batches did not carry, so Haiku judged them on the name alone. Waiting on the owner: fetch the article texts and rerun those (Haiku) before the hand reads (150 now) and before step 3. Files in the session scratchpad (vet/). 1. **Haiku, no web: sort every remaining name.** Batches of about 25 articles (7 agents), each given the article's title, outlet, place, summary, its names and up to 5 look-alike records (id, name, place, status, from `kop_facdisc_lookalikes()`). For the 69 articles with no names, first pull the program and company names from the title and summary. Verdict per name: `same_record` (an id from the look-alikes only), `other_era` (an id), `new_facility`, `new_company`, `young_adult`, `out_of_scope` (which rule), `not_a_program` (vague, a person, a place); confidence; the quote it rests on. JSON out, nothing sent. 2. **Lead checks Haiku.** By script: every id is one of that name's look-alikes, every quote is in the article text. By hand: every `same_record` whose names differ by more than a suffix, every low-confidence verdict, and 1 in 10 of the rest. A batch with more than 3 wrong in its sample is rerun on Sonnet. 3. **Sonnet, with web: research the candidates for new records.** Only `new_facility`/`new_company` (expect 40-80), about 10 per agent. Per name: did it exist; city, state; operator; type; years; status; other names; 2+ sources; a KOP duplicate check (`/mobile/check`, the look-alikes); the standing rules on submitting new sources (agents without the research key write a not-sent JSON; lead sends with `send-sources.py`) and on Wayback copies. Output in the Facilities from News create fields. 4. **Owner review on Facilities from News**, not a file: a one-time pass files each verdict on the name's card (`news_facility_candidates`): `same_record` -> "possible duplicate" with the record offered; `new_*` -> "To decide" with the researched fields prefilled for Create and the sources listed; out of scope / not a program -> their decisions with the reason, Undo kept. Card shows "Vetted by Claude: <verdict>, <evidence>". Needs a small card addition (the vetting note) before the pass. 5. **After the owner's decisions**: links follow (Link, Create); report how many articles still link to nothing and why. Cost: about 7 Haiku + 5-8 Sonnet agents; the lead's checks are scripts plus about 40 hand reads. Worklist scripts were in the session scratchpad (2026-10-28); step 0 rebuilds them as `scripts/news-name-vetting.php` (kop-pipeline if it only reads the mirror).

Built: three card kinds (Decide with one-click choice buttons, Do with Open buttons, Check with Looks right / Something is wrong), `Why:` / `Go:` / `Choices:` / `Time:` / `Step:` / `Focus:` lines in the plan files (docs/PLAN.md "Plan Board"), steps with only the next one shown ("Done, next", Skip, progress, All steps), the hourly check's evidence on the card while not done ("Now: 12 left"), Edit (headline, why, text; shown at once, row `<id>@edit`) and Retire (off the board at once) on every card, views This week (Focus) / Everything for you / Waiting for Claude / Whole plan and a kind filter. items.lead: One card per fact: clear what we hold, fold the rest together
items.text: **One card per fact: clear what we hold, fold the rest together** (owner, 2026-11-02: "scan all pending facts, compare to facts we already have on hand, and clear ones that are saying essentially the same thing; condense facts from multiple sources into one entry each"). Waiting on the mirror (tmp/prod.sqlite, 2026-11-02): Woodbury Facts 8,115 (Woodbury, HEAL, wiki, program papers; 1,739 on a record, 6,376 on 2,075 program names with no record), Fornits 12,376 (7,013 links, 1,882 staff, 1,365 incidents, 1,352 testimony, 764 leads), Facts from news 530. The hourly `kop_wbf_clear_on_record()` already files what the record holds word for word or by `kop_wbf_list_covers()`; what it misses: (a) the 3,567 **held** items (approved, waiting for a write-up, not on the record yet), so a second telling of a held fact still waits; (b) paraphrases (Provo Canyon, #10371: the May 2026 jaw injury is five cards from five articles, 84 incident cards in all); (c) copies among the waiting items themselves and across the three queues; (d) the no-record items. Read `docs/DATA-FLOWS.md` first (new status, new undo path). In order: a. **Measure, no writes**: `scripts/fact-dedupe.php --db=tmp/prod.sqlite` counts, per queue and kind, what each step below would clear or fold, with 20 examples each, so the owner reads a sample before anything changes. b. **"On hand" = record + held + approved**: before `kop_wbf_on_record()` runs, lay the record's held items (`status = 'held'`, `applied_fid`) and the other queues' approved items over a copy of its doc, the way `kop_wbf_doc_apply()` would write them. Staff by `kop_dd_same_person()`, incidents by `kop_dd_same_event()` (same kind, same month), Fornits links by the normalized URL against `resourceLinks` and the news links. A different value stays a conflict (Review inbox > Conflicts), never cleared. c. **Group the waiting items**: candidates share the record (or the program name key, for no-record items), the path and, for incidents, the year-month; staff share the person key. Inside a candidate group the rules decide first (`kop_wbf_text_same()`, `kop_dd_same_event()`); what is left close (same month, shared words) goes to (d). Groups never cross records, and never join items whose numbers, dates or names differ. d. **AI for "the same in other words"**: one call per record through `kop_ai_generate_alternating()`, logged as AI usage and within the daily budget: the record's lines (doc + held) and the waiting lines, numbered; answer per waiting line `same_as <n>`, `new` or `differs` (`differs` = a conflict). Cached by the lines' hash so a rerun costs nothing. AI only judges; it never writes the wording. e. **Condense**: each group keeps one item, the line with the most detail (the owner can edit it), and takes every other item's citation into its `evidence` list (already a list: 374 items carry two Woodbury citations). The others get status `merged` with `extra.merged_into` = the kept pkey; a news fact or Fornits item folded into a Woodbury item records it the same way (`news_facts.route = 'merged'` + `wbf_pkey`). The kept item's write-up cites every source. `kop_wbf_sync()` must keep folded citations when a reload rewrites a waiting item, and must not bring a `merged` item back. f. **Where they show**: cleared items go to the Rejected tab with the reason ("held for the write-up: <line>", "already on the record: <line>"), as the hourly clear does; merged ones to a "Folded together" view under the kept card. Both have Undo (Recently done): back to waiting, citations taken off the kept item, never cleared again. Items a person edited or sent back are left alone. g. **Run**: owner reads the sample from (a); then live in time-boxed chunks on the hourly hook after `kop_wbf_clear_on_record()`, rules first, AI second. Tests: a Provo Canyon fixture in `scripts/test-review-on-file.php` (five tellings fold to one with five citations; a held telling clears the sixth; a different date stays a conflict; Undo restores all). AI-judged copies are cleared at once like the rule ones, no confirm tab (owner, 2026-11-02); Undo is the check. **(a) done 2026-11-02**: `scripts/fact-dedupe.php --db=tmp/prod.sqlite [--facility=N] [--examples=N] [--json=...]` (read only, 6 s). Of 21,030 waiting: 522 Fornits already on the record (Fornits' own on-file rule; Woodbury's hourly clear is at 0), 22 covered by held items, 638 fold by the rules (Woodbury 109, Fornits 529, nearly all staff), up to 747 more if every AI candidate matched (993 lines, 162 calls, about 95-132k tokens). Woodbury held items cover pending ones only as paraphrases, so (b) does little for Woodbury and (d) matters most; the Provo jaw injury does not fold by the rules (dates "2026-05-14" / "2026-05" / none, other words), only by (d). Fixes the numbers call for before (b)-(g): - **Bug, live now**: `kop_wbf_text_core()` strips a trailing URL together with the citation's closing ")", so the citation is never taken off and two unrelated notes from one article compare as the same on its words (feeds `kop_wbf_list_covers()` and the hourly clear). Fix, test, then rerun (a). - `kop_dd_same_event()` joins different events of one kind and month (Provo: the 2026-07-06 Springville and 2026-07-17 Provo campus revocations); a different place or day must keep them apart. - Folding needs numbers equal on both sides and no clashing dates (the script's rule; 44 pairs `kop_wbf_text_same()` calls the same fail it). - Staff folds mostly join different roles (421 of 473 Fornits): the kept entry takes the role history; never fold "III"/"Jr." against the plain name. - News facts: 533 of 539 have no facility_id, so they join nothing; routing them to records comes first. - Not yet measured: Fornits testimony (1,352), approved Fornits/news items as "on hand", name variants of no-record programs ("Teen Challenge" / "Teen Challenge of Florida"). **Fixed 2026-11-02 (in the working tree, not committed yet)**: `kop_wbf_text_core()` keeps the citation's ")" when it strips the URL; `kop_dd_same_event()` keeps two named campuses apart (`kop_dd_campuses()`: only "X campus/facility/location/site/..."; a general place rule broke the Nidorf and AYA joins). Tests in `scripts/review-inbox-tests/record-cleanup.php` and `woodbury-facts.php`; the full `test-review-inbox.php` passes (1561). Rerun: Woodbury on-record 0 -> 13 (read, right), fold 109 -> 108. - **Wrongly cleared, restored as code (2026-11-02)**: `fact-dedupe.php --recheck-cleared` (now prints row ids) finds 11 Woodbury notes the hourly clear rejected on the bug (rows 27710-28735 on #100574, #100547, #13002, #100386, #100207, #13358, #100214, #12860, #100684, #13431 x2). `kop_wbf_restore_wrongly_cleared()` on the hourly hook puts them back to pending once (reviewed_by empty, so later folding still sees them), option `kop_wbf_restored_1102` = {restored, at}. Done on live 2026-11-02 19:15 UTC: restored 11, all 11 pending on the 15:06 mirror, the recheck shows only row 15173. #10618 (row 15173, pastOperators "Universal Health Services") checked by hand: stays rejected, the wiki says UHS runs it today and the record has it as `currentOperator`. - Still open: `kop_wbf_text_same()` ignores full dates and campuses, so the live clear can still call two same-month revocations worded alike "the same"; `kop_dd_campuses()` reads "Mount Hope campus" as "Hope". **Compare facts, not queues or fields** (owner, 2026-11-02: the same fact comes from Woodbury, news, the wiki, Fornits...). Today only one group crosses queues: news facts have no record (533 of 539), Fornits lines are worded in their own shape, and grouping is by field (a closure as a note vs `set_closed`, a founder in a note vs staff). Before (b)-(e), every item from every source becomes one shape (kind: staff, incident, closure, opening, name, owner, size; subject; date; place; record), and grouping and "on hand" use that shape. News facts get a record first (the exact-name rule of `inc/auto-connect.php`); facts of news articles already linked to the record count as on hand. A folded entry cites every source. Extend `fact-dedupe.php` to count groups that mix sources. **Shape specified and built 2026-11-02** (`docs/claude/fact-shape.md`): `inc/fact-shape.php` (read only, loaded on live), `kop_autoconn_exact_record()` + `kop_autoconn_name_index_of()`, `kop_nf_record_for()`, the `kop_nf_parse_reply()` fix (a fact with no record takes the exact-name record only among the article's linked ones), `fact-dedupe.php` on the shape (`--shapes`, the 7.2 news table, mixed-source groups), 39 fixtures in `scripts/review-inbox-tests/fact-shape.php`; suite 1600 pass. Run the suite with `-d memory_limit=1G < /dev/null` since the 11-02 15:06 mirror. Rerun on that mirror: fold 795 (Woodbury 126, Fornits 669; old script 637), held-covered 20, Fornits on record 521; news 20 of 542 linked, 2 ambiguous; 60 of 355 groups mix sources (fornits+record 32, heal+woodbury 10, wiki+woodbury 7, heal+wiki 6). Builder's own calls to check in the sample: first names match on three letters (+ a loose surname prefix for founder vs staff, "Art Barker" / "Arthur Robert Barker"); undated incidents of one category are AI-close on two shared words; Fornits investigation/lawsuit leads are incident facts. **Check after deploy**: the next news reads file facts naming a linked program on that record (Review inbox > Facts from news shows fewer with no record). **Owner, 2026-11-02: "just fold everything"**: no sample review, no confirm step; (b)-(g) run live on the hourly hook, Undo is the check. Being built in two passes: the fold engine with rules, the merged status, Undo, "Folded together", `kop_wbf_sync()` keeping folds, and the live news link (`inc/fact-fold.php`, `kop_nf_link_waiting()`); then the AI step (d) inside it. Then a dry run on the mirror, deploy, and a check of the first hourly runs. **Pass 1 built 2026-11-02 (working tree, not committed)**: `inc/fact-fold.php` (`kop_fold_run()`, `kop_fold_hourly()` on its own hourly event `kop_fold_hourly_event`, half an hour after the Woodbury clear, `kop_nf_link_waiting()` on the auto-connect and before the fold, Undo for all three queues), the `merged` status and "Folded together" views, `kop_wbf_sync()` keeping folds, write-up and Fornits lines citing every source; `scripts/fold-dry-run.php` (= `fact-dedupe.php --engine`); `scripts/review-inbox-tests/fact-fold.php`. Dry run on the 15:48 mirror: Fornits cleared 554 (521 on the record + 33 held, 13 more than the measurement: approved Fornits items now count as on hand), folded 779 (Woodbury 126, Fornits 653; measurement 795), 20 news facts linkable. Still open: the AI step (built 2026-11-03, below; 4,519 candidate pairs on the mirror), deploy and a look at the first hourly runs (Recently done lists each fold), a kept staff card does not yet take the folded members' roles (their lines are listed on it). **AI step (d) built 2026-11-03 (working tree, not committed)**: `kop_fold_ai_judge()` in `inc/fact-fold.php`, on the hourly run after the rules (`kop_fold_run(true, 90, array('ai' => 'live'))`): one call per record (40 lines a prompt at most), job "Fact fold: same in other words", 10 calls a run, budget checked before each, answers cached per line (option `kop_fold_ai_<md5 unit>`), put-off records on `kop_fold_state.ai_todo`. `differs` = a Conflict mark on the card, not the Conflicts tab. `kop_fold_ai_apart()` overrules an AI "same" over other dates, numbers, ages, places, people or incident types. `fold-dry-run.php --ai-estimate` on the 11-02 mirror: 160 calls, 3,386 lines (1,198 asked), ~306k tokens, 16 hourly runs. `--ai --facility=10371` (3 calls, nothing written): the five jaw-injury tellings judged one event (plus the Jezebel and Hollywood Reporter tellings); the neglect and investigation lines stay apart (type rule); Milonas/Rice = Milonas v. Williams; 3 AI "same" overruled, 1 differs. Tests in `scripts/review-inbox-tests/fact-fold.php` (stubbed AI). - **Check after deploy**: AI Usage shows the job, at most 10 calls an hour; Recently done lists AI folds ("(ai)"); read a sample of AI clears on the Rejected tabs and AI folds under Folded together, and the Conflict marks; `kop_fold_state.ai_todo` shrinks to 0 within about a day. - Open: AI conflict marks are only on the card, not on Review inbox > Conflicts (that tab settles record-vs-item values; a "which telling is right" action would be new). A Fornits card's mark is lost when a person's Undo rewrites `applied`; the cached answer puts it back on the next run. - **First live pass, 2026-11-03 16:30 UTC** (rules only; the AI step deployed at 16:36, so it starts with the next pass after the 3-hour pause, about 19:30 UTC): all 2,690 records in one run; 20 news facts linked; Fornits cleared 632 (574 staff already listed, 38 held, 17 links, 3 record); folded 864 (Fornits 734: staff 520, incident 131, closure 79; Woodbury 130: staff 56, incident 33, founder 14, ages 10). Dry run said 554 / 779. A sample of 16 folds read right (name variants, the same event worded twice). Staff folds join different roles and surname changes (Longnecker-Selby into Longnecker-Harper; Rob Crawford CEO into Robert Crawford owner): the kept card lists the folded lines, the record's staff entry does not take the roles yet. - **Check after the AI pass** (mirror after about 20:00 UTC, then a day later): `kop_fold_ai_*` options appear, AI Usage shows "Fact fold: same in other words" at most 10 calls an hour, `kop_fold_state.ai_todo` reaches 0. items.lead: Provo Canyon School's view reorders its rows when one line leaves
items.text: **Provo Canyon School's view reorders its rows when one line leaves** (found 2026-10-26 working item 6, now in PLAN-ARCHIVE). One staff line leaving the live records (Fitisemanu II - Provo Canyon School, kop-data f649268 -> 8d8af9a) moved the view's median line from 571px to 654px (the 2026-10-26 full run after the fix and a probe agree on 654px; the run before the fix printed 674px, unexplained). The bound in `scripts/test-network-modules.js` is now 720px with the reason written above it. Look at why the row order in focus.js is that sensitive (a stable tie-break, or ordering rows by what they connect to), and whether the 674px run points to state carried over from earlier checks. Read 2026-11-01 (no code changed; the 2026-11-01 full run passes at 654px again): a tie-break would not help, the keys are floats. orderRow() sorts a row by where each name's neighbours sit on the row already placed, and a name with no neighbour there falls back to the x the force settle left it at (`keys[p.id] = n ? sum / n : p.x`). The settle starts from `seed`, which for a new view is positionOf(node), where the previous view drew each name (settleLayout(), the `from` argument). So the order depends on what was on screen before, which fits the 674px run (state carried over from earlier checks), and one line fewer moves the whole settle, so the unanchored names reorder. A fix to weigh: seed the unanchored names from something stable (their own two-step neighbours' order, or the map's positions) instead of the last view, so the same graph always draws the same rows. Checked 2026-11-02: that is not it. For a click, seedCluster() places every name in the view by hand (fan rows round the click, then each two-step name beyond what it hangs off), overwriting the `seed` positions, so the last view never reaches the settle. A new check in test-network-modules.js draws Provo Canyon School, opens WWASPS, draws it again and compares every name's position: identical (median 654px both times). The same graph does draw the same rows. What one line changes is the hand seed itself (fanRows' order and each anchor's `hung` offsets follow the edge list), then 220 ticks of the force settle, then shelve() cutting rows by y; a small change upstream moves names across a row cut, and orderRow() then sorts the unanchored ones by settled x. Making that insensitive to one line is a layout redesign (e.g. rows by graph distance from the click instead of by settled y), not a tie-break: owner's call whether it is worth it. The 674px run stays unexplained; not reproduced.
